column9: contract_notes
Null admission, bounds and equality follow each existing overload.
Existing M3JDK21 text helper; String remains payload and Unicode semantic owner.
Array overloads retain range, primitive total-order and reference-array contracts.
Adapters retain their documented backing, synchronization and mutation policies.
Explicit finite sorting selection from the separate qualified sorting packet; Arrays defaults retained.
Sequential borrowed collection, iterable, iterator, enumeration and optional entry points; primitive overloads retained.
Borrowed resources; no close/flush; bounded requests and exact-read prefix behavior; explicit charset.
Literal modifier masks; detached member list; only caller-supplied Lookup authority; no accessible-flag mutation.
Existing overflow, NaN, signed-zero and numeric overload contracts remain authoritative.
Specified reproducibility requirements differ from Math where the existing API states so.
32-bit signed values and explicitly unsigned operations share the established Integer owner.
64-bit signed values; unsigned interpretation is explicit per operation.
Immutable arbitrary-precision integer owner; division/modulus and sign rules stay local.
Decimal scale, rounding and equals-versus-order distinctions remain explicit.
Distinguishes UTF-16 code units and Unicode code points; no new character facade.
Mutable text buffer with existing capacity, index and synchronization contract.
Compiled regex syntax and Matcher execution remain with the established regex owner.
Unicode normalization form is supplied explicitly.
Charset lookup and configurable encoder/decoder errors retain provider contracts.
Named guaranteed charset constants; no platform-default charset substitution.
Locale identity, language tags and installed locale data retain existing behavior.
Locale-sensitive ordering is distinct from Unicode or String lexical order.
Locale-aware mutable formatter; parsing, rounding and thread-use rules remain local.
Immutable date/time formatter; resolver, locale and zone rules are explicit.
UTC timeline values with existing range and overflow rules.
ISO calendar dates have no implicit time zone until an operation supplies one.
Time-based duration owner; conversion overflow remains documented by the existing API.
Zone identifiers and rule-provider data remain with the existing time API.
Clock injection and fixed/offset clocks support explicit time sources.
Factories create established temporal adjusters; chronology support follows target temporals.
Named random-generator creation; algorithm properties and seeds remain explicit.
Basic, URL and MIME variants retain their distinct alphabets and validation rules.
Immutable hex formatting/parser configuration; delimiter and case are explicit.
Existing UUID generation/version and parse contracts; no universal identifier registry.
Ordering composition remains distinct from equals; null policy is explicit.
Traversal adapters retain source characteristics, bounds and primitive specializations.
Absence and lazy fallback remain the existing value-based Optional contract.
Established JDK List owner; nulls, duplicates, backed sublists and fail-fast limits retained.
Resizable bits indexed by nonnegative integers; no object-lifecycle semantics implied.
Generated ByteBuffer type from X-Buffer.java.template; position, limit, byte order and shared-storage views remain explicit.
Provider, charset, link and stream-close contracts stay with Files and returned resources.
Retained path factory; Path is the path-value owner and Files owns file operations.
Provider-specific path values; lexical normalization does not resolve filesystem symlinks.
Filesystem-provider discovery and ownership of created filesystems remain explicit.
Terminal capabilities and borrowed console handles retain existing owner behavior.
Random-access ZIP owner; caller closes archives and acquired streams as documented.
JAR metadata, multi-release selection and verification retain the existing owner.
Mutable CRC-32 checksum state; this is not a cryptographic digest.
URI syntax and normalization do not perform network access.
HTML form encoding; use explicit Charset overloads; not general URI path escaping.
HTML form decoding retains plus-space and malformed-input rules.
Name service and address construction retain resolver and network behavior.
HTTP client configuration, response bodies, resources and asynchronous failures retain owner contracts.
Provider-selected message digests; algorithm choice remains explicit.
Signature algorithm, key admission and mutable operation state retain provider semantics.
Security-provider randomness; initialization and blocking follow the chosen provider.
Transformation, keys, parameters and authentication failures remain explicit.
Provider-backed symmetric key generation, without a new key store or global secret cache.
Executor factory ownership and task/close behavior retain each existing executor contract.
Completion, executor selection, cancellation and exception wrapping remain the existing contract.
Time conversions retain saturation/truncation; blocking helpers retain interruption semantics.
Permit and spurious-return rules remain explicit; parking is not monitor ownership.
Atomic int updates and memory-order variants remain with the existing atomic owner.
Existing M3JDK21 progress factories; borrowing and cancellation follow the established monitor API.
Provider discovery remains module/class-loader scoped with existing lazy failure behavior.
Locale fallback and resource-loader/cache rules stay with ResourceBundle.
Established capability factory; Reflections borrows explicit Lookup instead of manufacturing one.
Process environment, clocks and primitive copy operations retain existing security and overlap contracts.
Explicit subprocess configuration; process I/O and lifetime remain caller-managed.
Scoped stack traversal and retained-class-reference options follow the established API.
Platform management discovery; implementation capabilities remain discoverable through MXBeans.
Logger hierarchy, levels and handler ownership remain unchanged.
JDBC driver discovery and connection ownership remain with standard JDBC APIs.
Parser configuration, external-resource access and validation are explicit caller choices.
Transformation providers and URI/resource resolution retain configured contracts.
XPath object model and resolver configuration stay with existing factories.
Schema language, source access and error handling retain explicit factory configuration.
XML signature provider, validation context and keys remain explicitly supplied.
Image plugins and cache/stream ownership follow existing ImageIO overloads.
Swing event-thread rules and callback exception behavior remain authoritative.
JavaBeans discovery and established cache controls; no replacement reflection cache.
Naming-provider configuration and context/resource ownership remain explicit.
User/system preference trees retain backing-store and failure contracts.
Existing RMI registry entry points; remote/security and network failures remain visible.
Discovers installed providers; the registry does not imply any script engine ships by default.
System tool discovery may return null when the corresponding tool is unavailable.
JFR recording configuration and resource lifetime remain the established recording contract.
Existing M3JDK21 collection factories reuse dense JDK owners and primitive-slot owners by contract.
Live write-through filtered views and detached stable unmodifiable snapshots; preserve duplicates and backing representatives.
Canonical read-only live collection and ordered-map owner; mutation refusal includes no-op requests.
Live write-through navigable owners retain null, comparator, stored-representative and bounded-range contracts.
One dynamic Object[] payload; nulls/duplicate references; prepared-mask stable compaction; standard List surface.
Existing dense long[] owner; capacity separate from size; positional values are not persistent handles.
Detached immutable long payload plus primitive index/offset metadata; stable ordering moves indices.
Resumable caller-buffer selection; aligned ordinal states, signed row IDs and duplicates; explicit Java/JNI backend.
Detached stable index selection from caller-precomputed unsigned byte masks; no Java callback enters JNI.
Signed strides and physical offsets address full-width state planes; explicit native selection with no hidden fallback.
Primitive long occurrence rows with original encounter order; shared canonical path-mask backend and alias admission.
In-place aligned slot/mask metadata operations; zero is a valid slot and flags are application metadata.
Existing long value owner plus aligned full-width state lane; detached generation-marked snapshots.
Generation-checked primitive state lanes; flags do not alter object headers, reachability or garbage collection.
Lazy unmodifiable outer partitions over backed subList ranges; no copied element payload.
Owner-thread aligned start/end/state arrays and detached sorted index snapshots; no retained Span/Entry objects.
